exposure: maternal lactation for preterm vs term infants
cohort: The study included milk samples from 27 mothers of very preterm infants (28 0/7 to 32 6/7 weeks GA) and 34 mothers of term infants (37 0/7 to 41 6/7 weeks GA).
finding: Longitudinal measurements showed small differences in macronutrient composition between preterm and term human milk at similar postnatal stages, but numerous differences at similar postmenstrual ages, with male infant gender associated with higher fat content, especially in preterm human milk.
followup_time: Four months for preterm human milk and two months for term human milk.
gest_age: Very preterm infants (28 0/7 to 32 6/7 weeks GA) and term infants (37 0/7 to 41 6/7 weeks GA).
